title: ONE LIKE A SON OF MAN.
paragraphs: ONE LIKE A SON OF MAN.
Empires rose like monsters from the sea.
Daniel saw them.

Beasts with iron teeth.
Claws that crushed nations.
Wings that carried pride across the earth.

Babylon.
Persia.
Greece.
Rome.
Power after power.
Each one roaring, devouring, promising eternity.
But every empire in Daniel’s vision had the same ending:
They fell.

Kings boast.
Flags rise.
Statues are built.
Then dust.
Daniel watched the chaos of history unfold like a stormy ocean—kingdoms clawing their way out of the waves.
And then…
Everything changed.
The courtroom of heaven opened.

“The Ancient of Days took His seat…
His clothing white as snow.” (Daniel 7:9)
Fire flowed from His throne.
Books were opened.
Judgment fell.
And the beasts lost their power.
But Daniel saw someone else approaching.
Not another beast.
Not another tyrant.
Not another empire built on blood.
He came with the clouds of heaven.

Human.
Yet more than human.

“I saw in the night visions, and behold, one like a Son of Man came with the clouds of heaven…
And to Him was given dominion and glory and a kingdom, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve Him.” (Daniel 7:13–14)
This kingdom would not collapse.

No invasion.
No corruption.
No fall of Rome moment.
An everlasting dominion.
Centuries later, Jesus walked dusty roads in Galilee and used a title for Himself again and again:
“The Son of Man.”
Not random.
Not poetic.
It was a claim.
The carpenter from Nazareth was saying:
I am the one Daniel saw.
The beasts of history still roar.

Empires still rise.
Governments still promise salvation.
Power still seduces the human heart.
But Daniel’s vision whispers a deeper truth:
History is not controlled by beasts.
History is moving toward a King.

A crucified King.
A risen King.
A returning King.
The Son of Man.
And when His kingdom fully comes, every counterfeit throne will bow.

Not to Rome.
Not to Washington.
Not to Beijing.
To Jesus Christ.
Friend, this is the hope beyond empires:
The kingdom of Christ cannot collapse.

Not your failures.
Not your past.
Not even death itself.

Repent.
Believe the Gospel.
The Son of Man who received the eternal kingdom also went to a cross to rescue rebels like us.
And everyone who belongs to Him will share in that kingdom forever.
So lift your eyes above the beasts of history.
The clouds are not empty.
The King is coming.
